S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder is a chronic depressive condition marked by a persistently depressed mood lasting at least two years in adults, accompanied by associated symptoms that create functional impairment. It often has a gradual course with fewer clear boundaries than episodic major depression, and it is distinguished clinically by its long duration, steady low mood, and enduring impact on work, relationships, and daily routines.

patient.stressor: Brad’s course began after a significant injury during a hiking outing forced him to scale back the active, project-filled retirement he had built around STEM mentoring, art-making, chess, and community events. He adapted with his usual engineering discipline at first, but over 3 years and 3 months a steady depressed mood, fatigue that rest did not resolve, and quiet hopelessness about aging gradually narrowed his participation in workshops, jam sessions, and travel plans. The impairment was milder because he still maintained basic routines and some creative work, yet his wife and primary care physician both noticed that he was functioning below his long-standing baseline. He received psychiatric care after raising the issue himself at a routine medical follow-up and accepting a referral for evaluation.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: I came in because I’ve started to feel, in a quiet but stubborn way, that the best version of my life is behind me and that no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I’m not in tears or anything dramatic, but there’s this low, gray tone running underneath everything, even when I’m in the studio or sitting across from my wife at dinner.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: I still get up, do the shopping, and tinker with projects, but even small things like setting up for a mentoring session or walking through a community event leave me worn out in a way a nap doesn’t really fix.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I still manage the basics at home, but I’ve stepped back from mentoring, community events, music gatherings, and travel plans enough that my weeks are much smaller than they used to be.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on since the hiking injury a little over three years ago, about three years and three months now.
